svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Signalling through a G-protein-coupled receptor."], [1, "Adrenaline binds the receptor on the outside of the membrane."], [3, "The receptor changes shape inside and activates the G protein: \u03b1 releases GDP and binds GTP."], [6, "\u03b1-GTP separates and moves to adenylyl cyclase, switching it on."], [8.5, "Adenylyl cyclase turns ATP into cAMP, the second messenger."], [11, "cAMP activates protein kinase A, which triggers the response, e.g. glycogen \u2192 glucose."], [14.5, "\u03b1 hydrolyses GTP to GDP and rejoins \u03b2\u03b3: the system switches off."]]
svg.title: G-protein-coupled receptor signalling
svg.desc: Adrenaline binds a G-protein-coupled receptor; the G protein alpha subunit exchanges GDP for GTP, activates adenylyl cyclase, which makes cAMP from ATP; cAMP activates protein kinase A for a cell response; alpha then hydrolyses GTP and rejoins.
svg.text: Example: adrenaline acting on a liver cell.

g.data-info: A membrane protein that crosses the membrane seven times. The signal binds outside; the shape changes inside.
A hormone or neurotransmitter such as adrenaline; it does not enter the cell.
Inactive with GDP bound. The activated receptor makes α swap GDP for GTP; α-GTP separates from βγ.
Activated by α-GTP; converts ATP into cyclic AMP (cAMP).
Carries the signal inside the cell and activates protein kinase A. One signal makes many cAMP: amplification.
Protein kinase A phosphorylates enzymes, e.g. starting glycogen breakdown in liver cells.

g.text: Amplification: one adrenaline molecule → many active G proteins → thousands of cAMP
The first messenger stays outside; cAMP is the second messenger inside.

g.data-info: α hydrolyses its GTP to GDP and rejoins βγ.
